_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for TLS certificate pins across all Birdo clients. Every pin below is base64(SHA-256(DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo)) - the same value OkHttp writes as `sha256/...`, Android's <pin digest="SHA-256">, the rustls verifiers in the desktop app, and the iOS URLSession PinningDelegate. Pins are on the CA CHAIN (intermediate/root), never the leaf, so a ~90-day leaf renewal never needs a client release.
_generated_by: measured with openssl against the live chains from FIVE independent vantage points on 2026-09-06 - a UK consumer ISP (the measuring workstation, 20:36Z), the production hub 46.225.112.237 (Hetzner, 20:38Z), GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 in Azure northcentralus (Mobile-Client Cert Pins run 34028683100, 10:53Z) and in Azure centralus (Desktop-Client Cert Pins run 34028720220, 10:54Z, whose log quotes the full chain it got) and this repository's own live job in Azure westus2 (run 34059860524, 2026-09-06 21:03Z, every chain printed in full) - with every host dialled under three client offers (default, RSA-only signature_algorithms, ECDSA-only) from the first two, and every pin cross-checked against the CA's published certificate. Each pin's own _verification names where it was seen; each host's chain_shape.vantages says what every vantage returned. NOT measured: the VPN nodes - their sshd was unreachable from the measuring workstation. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-08 23:26Z, read-only openssl from two of those vantages (the UK ISP workstation and the production hub) for dns.google (three offers, both addresses) and cloudflare-dns.com (six client offers; four IPv4 addresses from both networks and both IPv6 addresses from the hub): the same chains and the same lineages as on 2026-09-06, recorded per host in chain_shape.vantages, together with this PR's own live job from Azure westus (run 34291599337, 23:39Z). scripts/check-cert-pins.sh --structure and scripts/test_check_cert_pins.py run on every push to every branch and on every pull request here.
_enforcement_rule: A connection is accepted if ANY certificate in the PRESENTED chain matches ANY pin for that host. A pin whose certificate the server does not send is dormant: it protects a future migration but can never satisfy today's handshake. Therefore every host MUST keep at least one pin that is present in the live chain. CHECKED: check-cert-pins.sh, rule E1.
_rotation_rule: ADD, NEVER SWAP. Add the new pin, ship it, wait for the fleet to adopt it, and only then remove the old one in a later release. Removing a pin that installed clients still rely on is unrecoverable - there is no remote kill switch for a bricked pin. Corollary: a pin added speculatively is effectively PERMANENT and must be transcribed identically into every enforcing client under an exact-set-equality gate, so do not add pins you have not measured. Retiring a pin is not machine-checkable on its own, which is why every removed hash must be recorded in _removed[] - CHECKED: check-cert-pins.sh, rule S5.
_overlap_rule: An intermediate and the root that signed it are ONE lineage: when a CA serves a host out of a different hierarchy BOTH die in the same handshake, so `intermediate + its own root` buys no migration safety at all - it only looks like two pins. Every pin therefore carries a machine-readable `lineage`, and every host must EITHER (a) declare >=2 distinct lineages AND (b) have >=2 lineages MEASURED LIVE - pins with in_live_chain: true from two different hierarchies, each actually seen presented by the server from some vantage or client offer - OR carry an explicit, dated `_overlap_risk` saying why not. Clause (b) counts LINEAGES, not live pins: dns.google's pre-outage set had TWO live pins (WR2 + GTS Root R1) in ONE lineage and nothing from GTS Root R4, and every user reaching an R4 edge lost the provider outright. A dormant pin from a second lineage does not satisfy (b): dormant means never yet seen presented, so it proves nothing about what the CA serves today. CHECKED: check-cert-pins.sh rules E2 (declared lineages) and E3 (live lineages); the exact pre-outage shape - WR2 + R1 live plus one dormant foreign-lineage pin - is a fixture in scripts/test_check_cert_pins.py and must keep failing.
_selection_rule: WHICH LINEAGE YOU ARE SERVED DEPENDS ON THE EDGE YOU REACH AND ON WHAT YOUR CLIENT OFFERS, SO ONE PROBE PROVES ONE LINEAGE. Every pinned host here is anycast. Measured 2026-09-06 for dns.google over the same addresses (8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4, SNI dns.google): a UK consumer ISP got leaf -> WR2 -> GTS Root R1 on 14 of 14 samples whatever the client offered (default, RSA-only and ECDSA-only signature_algorithms); the production hub 46.225.112.237 got leaf -> WE2 -> GTS Root R4 on 12 of 12 default and ECDSA-only samples, and leaf (*.google.com) -> WR2 -> GTS Root R1 on 2 of 2 RSA-only samples; GitHub Actions in Azure northcentralus matched WR2 (Mobile-Client run 34028683100, 10:53Z) while Azure centralus got WE2 / GTS Root R4 and FAILED against the old set (Desktop-Client run 34028720220, 10:54Z, chain hashes in its log), and Azure westus2 got WR2 / GTS Root R1 under both a default and an RSA-only offer (this repository's live job, run 34059860524). So selection is deterministic per (edge, client offer) - per-connection randomness has NOT been observed - and a rustls client, which offers ECDSA, gets R4 from an R4-serving edge every time. Three consequences: (a) `in_live_chain: true` means 'measured present from the vantage points named in _verification', never 'present everywhere'; (b) one network cannot certify a host - the UK vantage alone returned one lineage 14 times running and would have graded the pre-outage set green; (c) the rule is MEASURE EVERY LINEAGE FROM MORE THAN ONE NETWORK AND MORE THAN ONE CLIENT OFFER, AND PIN ONLY WHAT WAS MEASURED. Pinning a CA's whole published issuing set instead (ten dns.google pins, this file at commit 5515868) was considered and rejected by the owner on 2026-09-06: _rotation_rule makes every pin effectively permanent and transcribed into every client, and a pin no server has been seen to present is a guess with a blast radius. The six unmeasured GTS siblings are recorded in _removed with never_shipped: true; re-adding one requires a measured chain and the vantage that saw it. CHECKED: check-cert-pins.sh --live dials every host with a default AND an RSA-only offer, prints the chain it got, names which declared lineage each chain belongs to and lists the declared lineages it did not observe; structure rule E3 requires two lineages measured live or a dated waiver.
_ci: WHAT ACTUALLY RUNS, and what does not. (1) birdo-shared/.github/workflows/cert-pins.yml job `structure` runs scripts/check-cert-pins.sh --structure AND scripts/test_check_cert_pins.py (the checker against known-bad fixtures, including the pre-outage dns.google shape) on every push to every branch and on every pull request here, with no path filter. Rule S7 additionally holds every 'CHECKED:' clause in THIS file to the set of rules the checker actually implements, and test_check_cert_pins.py holds that set to the rule tags check-cert-pins.sh really emits - so a control cannot be deleted while its advertisement here survives, which is the failure this _ci key itself used to be an example of. (2) The same workflow's `vendor` job - push to main, daily 06:47 UTC, manual - fetches every copy listed in _consumers and fails if any has drifted from this file. It is the only control anywhere that can see 'SSOT ahead of the shipped clients', it is deliberately allowed to go RED while a fix is in flight, and it IS red today on two counts: Desktop-Client, Mobile-Client and birdo-web all still carry the pre-fix schema-2 copy, and birdo-web is private so the job also fails on auth until the CONSUMER_READ_TOKEN secret is set. (3) The `live` job - pull requests that change cert-pins.json, the checker, its tests or the workflow, plus daily and manual - dials every host with two client offers from the runner's vantage and prints the chain it got, so a runner log is a measurement record. It grades a host it could not dial at all as UNMEASURED and exits 3, not 1: a pin that no longer matches means an installed population cannot connect, while an unreachable third-party anycast address from one runner says nothing about the pins either way, and grading them the same is how the one check whose red matters becomes background noise. Both are still non-zero - an unmeasured host is not evidence the pins are good. (4) Desktop-Client and Mobile-Client each run their own scripts/check-cert-pins.sh: its check 2 (per-platform pin files vs that repo's OWN vendored copy) and check 3 (live chain) do run, but its check 1 (vendored copy vs this file) is SKIPPED on every CI runner, because those workflows check out a single repo and ../birdo-shared never exists there. So a green client run does NOT mean that repo agrees with this file - only control (2) tests that.

ONE live lineage: this is a Cloudflare edge certificate and Cloudflare chooses the issuing CA at each renewal - see _overlap_risk.

chain_shape._note: The served WE1 certificate is issued by GTS Root R4. The copy Google publishes at https://i.pki.goog/we1.crt is the GlobalSign ECC Root CA - R4 CROSS-SIGN of the same key: same SPKI, so one pin covers both, but they are different certificates with different issuers. Do not read an issuer off i.pki.goog and record it as the live hierarchy - the whole WE family is published there as GlobalSign cross-signs.

_overlap_risk.why: Only the GTS Root R4 lineage is measured live (WE1 + GTS Root R4, both presented). The isrg-x1 pins are dormant: real Let's Encrypt certificates, never yet seen serving this host, and the GlobalSign cross-sign anchor is never sent. That is the same shape that took dns.google dark, and it is graded here as a risk, not OK. The certificate is issued through Cloudflare, which selects the CA at each ~90-day renewal (leaf_expires 2026-11-27) from the pool it publishes for Universal SSL - Google Trust Services (pinned, live), Let's Encrypt (pinned, dormant) and SSL.com (NOT pinned). A renewal that lands on SSL.com bricks every installed client's API access with no remote recovery path. The zone's current CA setting was NOT checked (it needs the Cloudflare credential, which was not read).
_overlap_risk.mitigation: Before the next renewal window (Cloudflare renews roughly 30 days before expiry, so from about 2026-10-28): either restrict the zone's Universal SSL certificate authority at Cloudflare so it cannot move to a CA this file does not pin, or measure and pin the SSL.com lineage. Neither is done as of 2026-09-06 - this waiver exists so that fact is in the file, not in someone's head. Daily check 3 in both client repos and --live here dial api.birdo.app and fail the day the chain changes: detection, not protection.

cloudflare-dns.com.note: DoH resolver, and the ONLY DoH provider Android has left (P6-CLI-A-06). Measured 2026-09-06 from three networks (a UK consumer ISP, the production hub 46.225.112.237 and a GitHub Actions runner in Azure westus2) against 1.1.1.1 and 1.0.0.1 under three client offers, and RE-MEASURED 2026-09-08 23:26Z from the UK ISP and the hub against 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1, 104.16.248.249 and 104.16.249.249 - plus 2606:4700:4700::1111 and 2606:4700:4700::1001 from the hub; the workstation has no IPv6 route - under six client offers (default, TLS 1.2-only, RSA-only signature_algorithms, ECDSA-only signature_algorithms, h2 ALPN, and TLS 1.2 with RSA-authenticated ciphers only): 50 of 50 handshakes that produced a certificate presented the SAME two certificates - leaf + SSL.com SSL Intermediate CA ECC R2 - and nothing else; the RSA-cipher-only offer was refused with alert 40 (handshake_failure) from both networks on every address, so there is no RSA certificate on the edge; SNI one.one.one.one gets the same chain and no SNI gets no certificate. The root is NOT presented. Consequence, stated plainly: exactly ONE of the three pins below is ever in the presented chain, and there is no MEASURED second pin to add. WHAT CERTIFICATE TRANSPARENCY SAYS CLOUDFLARE HOLDS for this exact name (crt.sh, queried 2026-09-08, unexpired, subject cloudflare-dns.com + *.cloudflare-dns.com): three certificates from SSL.com SSL Intermediate CA ECC R2 (the presented lineage, the latest expiring 2026-12-22), one from SSL.com RSA SSL subCA (2026-01-15 to 2027-01-15), and one each from Google Trust Services WE1 and WR1 (2026-07-08 to 2026-10-06). None of the last three has been seen on the wire from any vantage or offer. They are the lineages a Cloudflare CA switch for this host would land on, and each becomes a pin here on the day --live or any other measurement sees it presented - not before: under _rotation_rule a pin is permanent and transcribed into every client, and a CT entry proves a certificate exists, not that an edge serves it. WHAT 'MATCHABLE' MEANS PER CLIENT: the desktop rustls verifier (doh.rs) hashes only end_entity + intermediates, so for it only the presented intermediate can match. Android's DohResolver pins through OkHttp's CertificatePinner, which checks the CLEANED chain - OkHttp's chain cleaner appends the trusted root from the device store when the server did not send it ('Add the trusted certificate to the end of the chain unless it's already present', BasicCertificateChainCleaner) - so on Android the SSL.com Root Certification Authority ECC pin is expected to match today (read from OkHttp's source, NOT device-tested). That root is the same lineage as the intermediate, dies in the same hierarchy switch and adds no overlap; it does mean an SSL.com re-issue under a NEW ECC intermediate keeps Android connected while it drops the desktop. The leaf (expires 2026-12-21) is deliberately not pinned: it is re-issued whenever the intermediate changes and so cannot protect against the rotation that matters. See _overlap_risk.

_overlap_risk.why: Three networks on 2026-09-06 and two again on 2026-09-08 - six addresses including IPv6, six client offers, 50 of 50 chains: Cloudflare presents leaf + SSL.com SSL Intermediate CA ECC R2 and never a root or a second CA certificate. Only that intermediate is in the presented chain. The two dormant pins are real certificates and correctly recorded, but neither is presented. Certificate Transparency shows Cloudflare also holds GTS WE1, GTS WR1 and SSL.com RSA certificates for this name (see note); none is served from any vantage, so none is pinned - under _rotation_rule a speculative pin is permanent and must be transcribed into every enforcing client - and the leaf is not pinned (see note).
_overlap_risk.mitigation: check-cert-pins.sh --live here (pull requests touching pins, daily) and check 3 in both client repos (daily) dial 1.1.1.1 and fail the moment the presented intermediate stops matching. That is detection, not protection: recovery still needs a client release. Android is less exposed than the desktop: OkHttp pins against the cleaned chain, so the SSL.com root pin also matches there and an SSL.com re-issue under a new ECC intermediate would not take Android down; it would take the desktop down (presented-chain hashing). Durable options, none taken yet: pin one of the CT-logged lineages (GTS WE1/WR1, SSL.com RSA subCA) the day a measurement shows it on the wire; get Cloudflare's issuing set for this host stated; or give Android a second DoH provider so this host is not its single point of failure.

dns.google.note: DoH resolver, desktop only. Android dropped this provider (P6-CLI-A-06). TWO HIERARCHIES, NOT ONE: Google Trust Services serves dns.google out of both an RSA hierarchy (leaf -> WR2 -> GTS Root R1) and an ECDSA one (leaf -> WE2 -> GTS Root R4), and which one a client gets depends on the anycast edge it reaches and on the signature algorithms it offers (_selection_rule). Measured 2026-09-06 over 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4: a UK consumer ISP got WR2 / R1 on every sample and every offer; the production hub got WE2 / R4 for default and ECDSA-only offers and WR2 / R1 for RSA-only; Azure centralus got WE2 / R4 and FAILED against the old set. Re-measured 2026-09-08 23:26Z from the same two networks: identical - the hub is still an R4 edge for a default or ECDSA-only client (4 of 4) and an R1 edge for an RSA-only one (2 of 2), the UK ISP is still an R1 edge under every offer (6 of 6). Until 2026-09-06 only the RSA lineage was pinned, so every user reaching an R4 edge got a hard pin failure and dns.google silently dropped out of the DoH pool. Both MEASURED lineages are now pinned - four pins, the intermediate and root of each - and nothing else: the sibling issuing CAs Google publishes (WR1/WR3/WR4, WE1/WE3/WE4) have never been seen serving this host and are recorded in _removed as never shipped. Read _security_note before changing this list in either direction.
dns.google._security_note: WHAT THIS PIN SET BUYS AND WHAT IT COSTS, stated because a posture change in a security file must not be silent. Pinning GTS Root R1 and GTS Root R4 means: any certificate for dns.google issued anywhere under either Google root is accepted. That is close to plain WebPKI for this host, and it is the availability trade the outage forced - a narrower set went dark for a whole population with no remote recovery path. The two ROOTS are what widen acceptance, and both are presented in a measured live chain, so they are not optional. Sibling intermediates under those roots would add NO acceptance surface (a chain through WR3 is accepted by the R1 pin anyway); they would only matter if Google started sending a SHORTENED chain (leaf + intermediate, no root), which it has never been observed to do for this host. The owner decided on 2026-09-06 NOT to pin them: under _rotation_rule a pin is effectively permanent and transcribed into every client, and a pin nobody has measured is a guess. If a shortened chain or a sibling intermediate is ever measured for this host, add THAT pin with its measurement. This is the only host here with two live lineages; do not copy its four-pin shape to a provider you have not measured serving two hierarchies.

No Quad9 CA rotation has been measured, and under _rotation_rule a speculative pin is permanent and must be transcribed into every enforcing client, so nothing is added on a guess. Recorded as an accepted, dated risk rather than graded OK.
_overlap_risk.mitigation: check-cert-pins.sh --live here (pull requests touching pins, daily) and check 3 in Desktop-Client (daily) dial 9.9.9.9 and fail on the day the intermediate changes. Detection, not protection - recovery needs a client release. The durable fix is to measure a DigiCert sibling G3 issuing CA actually serving this host and pin it, or to drop the provider.

Desktop-Client PR #125 carries this file's four-pin dns.google set; its third_party/cert-pins.provenance.json records which birdo-shared commit it vendored, and that repo's check 1b FAILS on every run - by design - while that commit is not on THIS repo's main. So #125 re-vendors and re-stamps from main after this file merges, and until #125 itself merges Desktop-Client main is stale and the vendor job here says so.
